label: weak: copy-phase input i late in long sequences (+ some L=9 delimiter steps)
explanation: Very sparse update-gate unit (0.26% of steps), never active in the original phase. About 58% of activation mass is on copy-phase steps whose input is i (16x lift), and about 24% is on the delimiter step, almost all at L=9. The strongest activations are copy-phase i inputs at recall_idx 3 or more in L=9 sequences. But it fires on only about 9% of copy-phase i steps and about 5% of L=9 delimiter steps, and no other variable tested (t, recall_idx, L, prev_tok) isolates which ones. The best predicate (copy-phase i, recall_idx>=3, L>=8) gets dev P=0.23, R=0.41, F1=0.29, mass recall 0.51. Adding the L=9 delimiter clause lifts mass recall to about 0.80 but drops precision to 0.07. Rare activations at other copy-phase inputs (s, y, a, ...). Not a coherent explanation.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, s, y, j, a, l; least: f, p, b, m) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: y, a, q, l; delimiter step: y, a, q, l; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9, L=8 & t=8, L=9 & t=9.
